topics.title: Disasters and natural hazards: meaning and changing perception

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of a disaster and identify disasters caused directly or indirectly by human actions.
Distinguish a natural hazard from a natural disaster and explain when a hazard becomes a disaster.
Explain how intensified human activity in hazard-prone areas has increased vulnerability.

topics.title: Classification of natural disasters and international efforts

concepts.learning_objective: Classify natural disasters as atmospheric, terrestrial, aquatic or biological.
Describe the Yokohama Strategy (1994) and the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
Explain why the Himalayan arc and parts of the Peninsula experience earthquakes.
Identify the earthquake damage risk zones of India and the regions in them.
Describe the effects of earthquakes and the preparedness measures to mitigate them.
Explain how tsunamis form and why their height increases in shallow coastal water.
Explain why tsunami losses are large and why mitigation needs international cooperation.
State the initial conditions needed for the formation of a tropical cyclone.
Describe where and when tropical cyclones originate around India.
Explain the consequences of tropical cyclones, including storm surge.
Explain the natural and human causes of floods.
Identify the flood-prone states of India and the types of flooding they face.
Evaluate the consequences of floods and the measures to control them.
Distinguish meteorological, agricultural, hydrological and ecological droughts.
Identify the extreme, severe and moderate drought-affected areas of India.
Explain the consequences of drought and its immediate and long-term mitigation measures.
Identify the landslide vulnerability zones of India and the factors controlling landslides.
Explain the consequences of landslides and area-specific mitigation measures.
Describe pre-disaster, during-disaster and post-disaster management stages.
